elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience..." — Statement of Work is this MSA's Order Form analogue, and the right is unconditional (no 'no uncompleted SOW' precondition), so it operates during an active engagement.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Contractor" — exactly 30 days, in writing, and no additional conditions or approvals attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case Contractor shall refund to Company, pro rata, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of such termination" — the words 'pro rata' are express, not inferred from the post-termination period alone.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained 6(a) confines the bilateral no-cause right to "At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding"; 6(b) is cause-based only, and the new sentence grants convenience rights to Company alone. Contractor therefore cannot exit while committed work (an outstanding SOW) exists.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice; no 60–90 day formulation appears (this is more favourable to us, but the fallback element as written is not satisfied).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 6 and the compensation provisions impose no early-termination fee or penalty on Company, and the redline adds none, so there is nothing requiring a three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Retained 6(a) lets Contractor terminate "for any or no reason" whenever no SOW is outstanding; the effective date is not tied to the end of any then-current term (the Agreement has no fixed term under Paragraph 2).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Contractor's 6(a) convenience notice remains fifteen (15) days; the redline does not extend it.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: the added sentence supplies an unconditional Company convenience right over the Agreement or any Statement of Work, 30 days' advance written notice, and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, while retained 6(a) already denies Contractor any convenience exit while an SOW is outstanding.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion, no deletions, no survival tail, no expense or damages language, and the drafter correctly omitted the model clause's surplus "in whole or in part" since no Order Form/partial-termination structure requires it.

Intent preserved: the sentence is introduced with "In addition", so 6(a)'s no-SOW bilateral right and 6(b)'s cure-based termination, the fees-through-termination payment mechanic and the Works-in-progress assignment all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.

Fallback is not independently complete (30-day Customer notice rather than 60–90; Contractor's 15-day right is not term-end-anchored), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Optional polish only, not required for completeness: if Contractor pushes back, the retained 15-day Contractor notice in the no-SOW shell period could be lengthened, and it would be worth confirming that 'prepaid fees' captures prepaid expenses/retainers under any Statement of Work.
